title: Admin - Assign Admin Role - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Assign Admin Role feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Super Admins to assign or change roles (Super Admin, Limited-Access Admin) via an editable role dropdown on admin cards. Changing a role automatically updates permissions, with instant save or confirmation. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for dropdown accessibility, keyboard navigation, screen reader announcements for role changes, error handling, and dynamic permission updates.

testCases.title: Role dropdown has accessible label identifying the admin
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Internal Administrators page is loaded with at least one admin card
steps: Navigate to an admin card's role dropdown using screen reader
Verify the dropdown has an accessible name that includes context (e.g., 'Role for John Doe' or 'Admin role')
Verify the dropdown announces its current value (e.g., 'Super Admin')
Verify the dropdown role is announced (combobox, listbox, or select)
expectedResults: Dropdown has an accessible name that identifies its purpose
If multiple role dropdowns exist on the page, each is distinguishable (includes admin name context)
Screen reader announces: name, role, and current value (e.g., 'Role for John Doe, combobox, Super Admin')
Label is programmatically associated via aria-label, aria-labelledby, or <label>
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users can identify which admin's role they are changing

testCases.title: Role dropdown is fully operable via keyboard
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Tab to the role dropdown on an admin card
Press Enter or Space to open the dropdown
Use Arrow Down to navigate to 'Limited-Access Admin'
Use Arrow Up to navigate to 'Super Admin'
Press Enter to select the focused option
Reopen dropdown, press Escape to close without changing
expectedResults: Dropdown is reachable via Tab key
Enter/Space opens the dropdown options
Arrow keys navigate between 'Super Admin' and 'Limited-Access Admin'
Enter selects the currently focused option
Escape closes dropdown without changing the role
No mouse interaction is required
testCases.postconditions: Role dropdown is fully operable via keyboard only

testCases.title: Role dropdown has visible focus indicator
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Tab to the role dropdown
Observe the focus indicator on the dropdown trigger
Open the dropdown and observe focus on individual options
Navigate between options using arrow keys
expectedResults: Dropdown trigger shows a clearly visible focus indicator
Focus indicator has at least 3:1 contrast ratio against adjacent colors
Individual options show focus/highlight when navigated via keyboard
Focus indicator is not solely a color change
testCases.postconditions: Focus state is clearly visible on dropdown and options

testCases.title: Dropdown expanded/collapsed state is communicated to screen readers
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role dropdown is available
steps: Focus on the role dropdown (closed state)
Verify screen reader announces 'collapsed' or equivalent
Open the dropdown
Verify screen reader announces 'expanded' or equivalent
Close the dropdown with Escape
Verify screen reader announces return to 'collapsed' state
expectedResults: aria-expanded='false' when dropdown is closed
aria-expanded='true' when dropdown is open
Screen reader announces state changes
State transitions are immediate and accurate
testCases.postconditions: Dropdown open/close state is always communicated

testCases.title: Role change is announced to screen readers
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with role dropdown is available
steps: Enable screen reader
Open the role dropdown on an admin card
Change the role from 'Super Admin' to 'Limited-Access Admin' (or vice versa)
Listen for screen reader announcement confirming the role change
Verify the new role value is reflected in the dropdown
expectedResults: Screen reader announces the role change confirmation (e.g., 'Role changed to Limited-Access Admin')
Announcement uses aria-live='polite' or role='status'
Dropdown displays the new role value
User does not need to move focus to confirm the change occurred
testCases.postconditions: Role change is communicated to assistive technology users

testCases.title: Permissions update is announced after role change
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with visible permissions is available
steps: Change an admin's role from 'Super Admin' to 'Limited-Access Admin'
Observe the permissions section update
Verify screen reader is informed that permissions have changed
Navigate to the permissions section and verify updated values
expectedResults: Permissions update is announced via aria-live region (e.g., 'Permissions updated for Limited-Access Admin role')
Updated permissions are reflected in the UI
Screen reader can read the new permission values
Change does not cause unexpected focus shift
testCases.postconditions: Permission changes are communicated accessibly

testCases.title: Confirmation dialog (if present) is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role change triggers a confirmation dialog
steps: Change an admin's role to trigger confirmation
Verify the confirmation dialog has role='dialog' or role='alertdialog'
Verify the dialog has an accessible name
Verify focus moves to the dialog
Verify the dialog has confirm and cancel buttons with accessible names
Press Escape to cancel
Verify focus returns to the role dropdown
expectedResults: Confirmation dialog has role='dialog' or 'alertdialog'
Dialog has accessible name (e.g., 'Confirm role change')
Focus moves into the dialog on open
Confirm and Cancel buttons have clear accessible names
Escape cancels the action and closes the dialog
Focus returns to the role dropdown after close
Dialog traps focus while open
testCases.postconditions: Confirmation dialog is fully accessible (if applicable)

testCases.title: Role change does not cause unexpected context change
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role dropdown is available
steps: Focus on the role dropdown
Change the role selection
Verify focus remains on or near the dropdown after the change
Verify no unexpected page navigation occurs
Verify no unexpected modal opens (unless it's a confirmation dialog)
expectedResults: Focus remains on the dropdown or moves predictably
No unexpected navigation occurs
If a confirmation dialog opens, it is expected and accessible
Page content updates in place without full reload
User maintains their context on the page
testCases.postconditions: Role change does not disorient the user

testCases.title: Last Super Admin downgrade prevention error is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, only one Super Admin exists in the system
steps: Attempt to change the last remaining Super Admin's role to 'Limited-Access Admin'
Verify an error message is displayed preventing the action
Verify the error is announced by screen reader immediately
Verify the error uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'
Verify the role dropdown reverts to 'Super Admin'
expectedResults: Error message is displayed clearly (e.g., 'Cannot downgrade the last Super Admin')
Screen reader immediately announces the error (role='alert' or aria-live='assertive')
Error does not rely solely on color (includes text and/or icon)
Error text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
Role dropdown reverts to original value
Focus remains on or returns to the dropdown
testCases.postconditions: User is clearly informed why the role change was prevented

testCases.title: Backend error during role change is accessible
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, backend is configured to fail on role change
steps: Attempt to change an admin's role (with backend failure simulated)
Verify an error notification is displayed
Verify the error uses role='alert' or aria-live='assertive'
Verify screen reader immediately announces the error
Verify the dropdown reverts to the previous role value
expectedResults: Error notification is visually displayed with clear message
Screen reader immediately announces the error
Error includes text (not just color indicator)
Error text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
Dropdown reverts to previous value (no inconsistent state)
User can retry the action
testCases.postconditions: Backend errors are communicated immediately and state is consistent

testCases.title: Role dropdown options have sufficient color contrast
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role dropdown is open
steps: Open the role dropdown
Use a contrast checker to measure text contrast of 'Super Admin' option
Measure text contrast of 'Limited-Access Admin' option
Check contrast of hover/focus state for options
Check contrast of the currently selected option indicator
expectedResults: All option text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
Hover/focus state maintains at least 4.5:1 text contrast
Selected option indicator has at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors
All text is readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: Dropdown options are readable

testCases.title: Selected role indicator does not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, role dropdown is open showing current selection
steps: Open the role dropdown
Observe how the currently selected role is indicated
View in grayscale mode
Verify the selected option is still distinguishable
expectedResults: Selected role uses more than color alone (e.g., checkmark, bold, background pattern)
In grayscale mode, selected option is still identifiable
aria-selected='true' or equivalent marks the current selection programmatically
testCases.postconditions: Selected role is perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: No keyboard trap in role dropdown
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin list is loaded
steps: Tab to the role dropdown
Open the dropdown
Press Escape to close
Tab away from the dropdown
Verify focus moves to the next element
Shift+Tab back to the dropdown
Verify focus returns correctly
expectedResults: Focus can enter and leave the dropdown freely
Escape closes the dropdown and focus remains on trigger
Tab moves focus to next element after dropdown
Shift+Tab returns focus to dropdown from next element
No keyboard trap exists at any point
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard users can freely navigate away from the dropdown

testCases.title: Role change loading state is communicated
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, about to change a role
steps: Change an admin's role
Observe if a loading/saving indicator appears during the save
Verify screen reader announces the saving state
Verify screen reader announces when save is complete
expectedResults: If a loading state is shown, it is announced via aria-live='polite' or role='status'
Screen reader announces 'Saving...' or similar during the operation
Screen reader announces completion (e.g., 'Role saved' or 'Role updated')
Dropdown is disabled or indicates busy state during save (aria-busy='true')
testCases.postconditions: Loading/saving state is communicated to all users

testCases.title: Role dropdown is functional at 200% browser zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify the role dropdown is fully visible on admin cards
Open the dropdown and verify all options are visible
Select an option and verify the change works correctly
Verify error messages (if triggered) are visible
expectedResults: Dropdown trigger is fully visible at 200% zoom
Dropdown options are not clipped or hidden
All option text is readable
Selection works correctly at 200%
Error messages are visible without horizontal scrolling
testCases.postconditions: Role dropdown is fully functional at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Role dropdown reflows at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify the role dropdown is accessible without horizontal scrolling
Open the dropdown and verify options are fully visible
Select an option and verify functionality
expectedResults: Dropdown adapts to narrow viewport
No horizontal scrollbar required to access the dropdown
Options are fully readable at narrow width
Functionality is preserved
testCases.postconditions: Role dropdown works on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Tab order is logical across multiple admin cards with role dropdowns
testCases.componentElement: Multiple role dropdowns across admin cards
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, multiple admin cards are displayed
steps: Tab through the page starting from the first admin card
Verify focus moves through each admin card's interactive elements in order
Verify role dropdowns are reached in the same order as the visual layout
Verify no dropdown is skipped or reached out of order
expectedResults: Tab order follows visual layout (first card's dropdown → first card's other controls → second card's dropdown → etc.)
No unexpected focus jumps between cards
All role dropdowns are reachable via Tab
Order is predictable and logical
testCases.postconditions: Keyboard navigation through multiple dropdowns is logical

testCases.title: Error messages do not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, a role change error has been triggered
steps: Trigger a role change error (e.g., downgrade last Super Admin or backend failure)
Observe how the error is indicated visually
View in grayscale mode
Verify the error is still identifiable without color
expectedResults: Error includes text message (not just red border or icon color)
Error has an icon or text prefix in addition to color
In grayscale mode, error is still clearly identifiable
Error state uses multiple visual cues
testCases.postconditions: Errors are perceivable regardless of color vision

testCases.title: Role dropdown touch target meets minimum size
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, page viewed on touch device or responsive view
steps: Measure the clickable/tappable area of the role dropdown trigger
Measure the clickable area of each dropdown option when open
Verify adequate spacing between the dropdown and adjacent interactive elements
expectedResults: Dropdown trigger has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Each dropdown option has at least 44x44 CSS pixels touch target
Adequate spacing exists between dropdown and adjacent controls (e.g., Edit Permissions button)
testCases.postconditions: Dropdown is usable for users with motor impairments

testCases.title: Role dropdown is within appropriate landmark region
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin page is loaded
steps: Use screen reader landmark navigation
Verify the role dropdown is within the main content landmark
Verify the dropdown is contextually associated with its admin card
expectedResults: Role dropdown is within the main landmark region
Dropdown is logically grouped within its admin card context
Screen reader users can locate the dropdown via landmark navigation
testCases.postconditions: Dropdown is discoverable within page structure
